samples.summary: Quadratic `snapFreezePastMerges` is now executed on every `POST .../insert` and `POST .../delete`, turning a cheap authenticated request into an event-loop-blocking CPU DoS on a document with many merges
samples.evidence: Attack: a caller with any write-scoped API key / editor access on one workspace document (1) uploads a large merge map via `PUT .../tabs/:tabId/merges`. `parseMerges` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:107) bounds each span's *cells* (`rs*cs <= 100000`) but places **no bound on the number of entries**, and the JSON body limit is 25MB (packages/backend/src/main.ts:20), so ~10^5–10^6 two-cell merges fit in one legal request. Entries are stored in caller-controlled order. (2) The caller sets a small freeze, then issues one `{axis:'row',index:1,count:1}` insert. The new line at worksheet-structure.ts:278 runs `snapFreezePastMerges` over the whole merge map inside the synchronous `doc.update` callback (packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:340-362). `snapFreezePastMerges` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:216-230) is a `while (changed)` loop over all entries; each pass allocates `parseRef`/`toMergeRange` per entry and only one boundary growth per pass is guaranteed. With a descending 'staircase' map (A1000:A1001, A999:A1000, ... A1:A2 submitted in that order) each pass advances the boundary by exactly one, giving O(n^2) — ~2.5e9 parseRef calls at n=50k, far more at n=500k. Node's single event loop is blocked for the whole time, so one request stalls every tenant on that backend instance, and it is repeatable and cheap. Before this delta the same primitive existed only on `PUT freeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:112); this delta newly puts it on the insert/delete path, where it also runs unconditionally even when the tab has no freeze at all (rows=cols=0 still materializes and scans the whole map).

samples.summary: `parseMerges` caps the cells per merge but not the number of merge entries, leaving the merge map an unbounded attacker-controlled input to every merge-walking code path (now including insert/delete)
samples.evidence: `parseMerges` validates each key and caps `rs*cs` at `MaxMergedCells = 100000` (line 148) precisely because `rebuildMergeCoverMap` walks span area; no equivalent cap exists on `Object.entries(merges).length`, so a single 25MB `PUT merges` body can store hundreds of thousands of entries. Every merge walk then scales with that: `assertMoveKeepsMerges`/`assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:154,192), `assertMergesClearOfFreeze` (worksheet.controller.ts:190), and now `snapFreezePastMerges` on every insert/delete (worksheet-structure.ts:278), the last of which is superlinear. Attacker cost is one request; server cost is unbounded CPU inside a synchronous `doc.update`.

samples.summary: The new snap writes `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` derived from merge data with no grid clamp, so insert/delete can persist a freeze above the `MaxRows`/`MaxColumns` ceiling `parseFreeze` exists to enforce
samples.evidence: `parseFreeze` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:54-60) rejects `rows > 1000000` / `cols > 18278` with the documented reason that an out-of-grid freeze makes the frozen quadrants allocate per frame so 'the UI never paints — which also means the user cannot reach the freeze menu to undo it'. Lines 283-288 assign whatever `snapFreezePastMerges` returns, which is the bottom/right edge of a merged block. `shiftMerge` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:65-98) applies no grid clamp, so an insert can push a block's end past the grid (e.g. merge anchored A999999 rs=2 with frozenRows=1000000, then insert one row at index 1 → snapped frozenRows=1000001), persisting through `POST .../insert` a freeze value the dedicated `PUT freeze` endpoint would reject. The same write also accepts spans a non-API writer (Yorkie collaborator, XLSX import) put in `ws.merges` unvalidated, e.g. a huge or non-finite `rs`, and turns them straight into the stored freeze. Impact is a client-side render/availability problem for every viewer rather than a server compromise, and the magnitude is largely reachable already via `PUT freeze`'s own snap, hence minor.

verdict.reason: Every cited element is present as described. snapFreezePastMerges (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:207-233) is a `while (changed)` loop with a full O(n) inner scan over all merge entries, allocating parseRef/toMergeRange per entry per pass and guaranteeing only one boundary growth per pass — genuine O(n^2) worst case. It is now invoked unconditionally on the insert/delete path at packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:278-282 (reached via applyWorksheetShift:611), which the backend runs synchronously inside doc.update at packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-structure.controller.ts:340-362. parseMerges (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:107-157) caps only per-span cells (line 148) and anchor coordinates (line 135) — I read the entire function and there is no cap on the number of entries — and the JSON body cap is 25MB (packages/backend/src/main.ts:20,48-57), so 1e5-1e6 entries fit in one legal authenticated request. I probed 'already-guarded': the REST endpoints do enforce non-straddling states (worksheet.controller.ts:184-200 assertMergesClearOfFreeze, :112 snap on PUT freeze, worksheet-structure.controller.ts:295), which makes the multi-pass staircase harder to build via REST alone, but these are per-endpoint checks rather than a storage invariant — the Yorkie document is written directly by clients (packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:481), so a straddling, adversarially ordered merge map is reachable with ordinary document write access. I could not demonstrate unreachability, and DoS via unbounded attacker-controlled input is not excluded by this lens, so the finding stays. (Minor softening: the no-freeze case costs only one O(n) pass, comparable to the shiftMergeMap scan already done at worksheet-structure.ts:598-606; the blocking concern is the multi-pass quadratic.)

verdict.reason: Verified independently: parseMerges (worksheet-settings.ts:107-157) caps per-merge area at MaxMergedCells=100000 (line 148) but never checks Object.entries(merges).length (loop at line 121, return at 156). Its only caller, PUT merges (worksheet.controller.ts:226-255), assigns the full map at line 249 inside a synchronous doc.update, with assertMergesClearOfFreeze (184-200) itself iterating every entry. I searched wide for a cap under another name: the backend's other resource caps are MaxClearedCells/MaxAxisEntries/MaxRows/MaxColumns (worksheet-structure.ts:11,12,30,56) and none bound the merge map; every backend reference to `merges` lives in these two files plus migration/spec code. No generic guard applies either — the handler takes `@Body() body: unknown`, so the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-72) has no metatype, the only size bound is JSON_BODY_LIMIT='25mb' (main.ts:20,50) which allows ~1e6 minimal entries, and the global throttler is 120 req/min (app.module.ts:102), which does not bound a single request's cost. The downstream walks are real and superlinear: snapFreezePastMerges materializes all entries and rescans them in a `while (changed)` loop (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:207-233), called on insert/delete at packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-structure.ts:278 and at worksheet.controller.ts:112, plus moveMergeMap/assertMoveKeepsMerges at worksheet-structure.controller.ts:154,192. Net effect: one authenticated write request stores an attacker-sized map that charges unbounded CPU to every later structure operation inside a synchronous doc.update, blocking the shared Node event loop for all tenants — unbounded resource allocation (CWE-770), major severity. The reviewer's only inaccuracy is the file path for line 278 (it is the sheets package, not the backend file), which does not affect the finding.
